'''''Carex trinervis''''' is a species of [[sedge]] which is native to Europe.

It is a perennial herb, which grows to a height of 40 cm, has glaucous leaves and spreads by stolons. It bears 2–3, sessile, oblong inflorescences per shoot.<ref>[https://www.tela-botanica.org/bdtfx-nn-14460-synthese Tela Botanica - Carex trinervis]</ref>

It is found in sandy [[marshes]], damp [[dune]] slacks and [[heaths]] in coastal areas of Western Europe.<ref>[https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/carex-trinervis Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora]</ref><ref>[https://www.tela-botanica.org/bdtfx-nn-14460-synthese Tela Botanica - Carex trinervis]</ref> In the British Isles it was only ever identified in [[Ormsby (disambiguation)|Ormesby]], Norfolk, where it became extinct in 1869.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.speciesrecoverytrust.org.uk/LostLife.html |title=The Species Recovery Trust - Lost Life |access-date=2019-07-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190428193658/http://www.speciesrecoverytrust.org.uk/LostLife.html |archive-date=2019-04-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/carex-trinervis Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora]</ref>
